title: Design System: Serhii Kushnir — Full Stack Dev Portfolio

display.purpose: Hero name and footer wordmark, always uppercase.

headline.purpose: Default h2 — section titles like Services, Let's connect.

title.purpose: h3 — project titles inside the dark showcase.

label.purpose: Breadcrumbs, index numbers, tech-stack chips, monospace UI labels.

signature.purpose: Reserved for the digital clock digits and the chat assistant's name only — never body content.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Filled pill CTA — the site's default action (Open CV, Book a free call).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #B8FF5B; color: #171717; border: none; border-radius: 9999px; min-width: 144px; height: 52px; padding: 0 24px; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 18px; line-height: 20px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s, transform 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #9BEF2D; transform: scale(1.03); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #B8FF5B, 0 0 0 4px #171717; }

components.name: Secondary Button (dark)
components.description: Outlined pill button used on console/void surfaces (e.g. 'Ask my AI assistant').
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary-dark { background: transparent; color: #FFFFFF; border: 1px solid #454545; border-radius: 9999px; height: 52px; padding: 0 24px; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 18px; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.2s, color 0.2s; } .ds-btn-secondary-dark:hover { border-color: #B8FF5B; color: #B8FF5B; }

components.name: Service Card
components.description: White rounded card with an icon chip and arrow affordance; the one place a hover shadow appears.
components.html:
●↗

Websites & Web Apps

Fast, accessible, production-ready builds.
components.css: .ds-card-service { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 24px; height: 100%; border-radius: 20px; background: #FFFFFF; padding: 24px; text-decoration: none; transition: transform 0.3s, box-shadow 0.3s; } .ds-card-service:hover { transform: translateY(-4px); box-shadow: 0 10px 30px rgba(0,0,0,0.12); } .ds-card-service__row { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; } .ds-card-service__icon { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 40px; height: 40px; border-radius: 8px; background: #B8FF5B; color: #171717; } .ds-card-service__arrow { color: #171717; opacity: 0.3; transition: opacity 0.3s, transform 0.3s; } .ds-card-service:hover .ds-card-service__arrow { opacity: 1; transform: translate(2px, -2px); } .ds-card-service__title { font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 18px; color: #171717; margin: 0; } .ds-card-service__desc { font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 16px; color: #171717; margin: 0; }

components.name: Chat Bubble (assistant)
components.description: Console-toned message bubble for the AI assistant's replies, squared toward the sender.
components.html: Happy to help — want me to open a project or book a call?
components.css: .ds-bubble-assistant { display: inline-block; max-width: 85%; background: #171717; color: #D1D1D1; border-radius: 16px; border-bottom-left-radius: 6px; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #454545; padding: 10px 16px; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.5; }

components.name: Chat Bubble (visitor)
components.description: Signal-lime message bubble for the visitor's own messages, squared toward the sender.
components.html: Do you build mobile apps too?
components.css: .ds-bubble-user { display: inline-block; max-width: 85%; background: #B8FF5B; color: #000000; border-radius: 16px; border-bottom-right-radius: 6px; padding: 10px 16px; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.5; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Void-background text input used in the chat composer and booking form.
components.css: .ds-input { height: 44px; width: 100%; border-radius: 9999px; background: #000000; color: #FFFFFF; border: none; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #454545; padding: 0 16px; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 16px; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #6E6E6E; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px #B8FF5B; }

components.name: Navigation Link
components.description: Header/footer nav item — plain text weight, no underline, lime focus ring.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-weight: 400; font-size: 16px; color: inherit; text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav-link:hover { opacity: 0.75; } .ds-nav-link:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #B8FF5B; border-radius: 4px; }

components.name: Tech Stack Chip
components.description: Monospace outlined tag used for tech-stack labels on the services page.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-block; border-radius: 9999px; border: 1px solid #D1D1D1; padding: 4px 12px; font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 10px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: #6E6E6E; }

narrative.overview:
This is a developer's own workbench, made presentable to clients: an off-white page that behaves like paper, interrupted by black console panels — the project showcase, the contact CTA, the chat sheet — where a single lime signal color does all the talking. The lime isn't decoration; it reads like a terminal cursor or a status LED, precise and technical rather than playful. It shows up sparingly — one button, one active state, one accent chip — and its rarity is what makes it register as "live."

Type carries the same logic. Space Grotesk, a geometric sans, is the one voice for everything a visitor reads: headlines, body copy, labels, buttons. A second, pixel-LCD monospace font is held in reserve as a signature — it only appears on the digital clock's numerals and the chat assistant's name ("Sonia"), like a device display glimpsed through the interface, never used for real content. Monospace labels (breadcrumbs, service index numbers, tech-stack chips) supply the "console" texture without needing a second typeface.

Surfaces are flat by default — no drop shadows, no gradients-as-depth, no glassmorphism beyond the header's backdrop blur. Depth comes from color contrast (paper vs. console vs. void) and from generous rounding: pill buttons, 16–20px card radii, circular avatars. The rounding is deliberate softness laid over an otherwise technical, grid-and-monospace base — approachable despite the terminal framing. The one place a shadow is allowed to exist is as a hover response on the service cards, never at rest.
keyCharacteristics: One accent color (lime), used sparingly against black consoles and an off-white page — never a second or third hue.
Space Grotesk for everything read; the pixel-LCD font is a rare signature, confined to the clock and the bot's name.
Flat at rest everywhere; the sole shadow appears only as a hover response on service cards.
Pill buttons and 16–20px card radii soften an otherwise monospace/technical, grid-driven structure.
Dark console panels (project showcase, contact CTA, chat sheet) interrupt an otherwise light, paper-toned page.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Lime appears on at most one interactive element's resting state per view (one primary button, one active chip) — everything else is neutral until it's hovered, focused, or selected. It is a status indicator, not a brand wash.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Space Grotesk carries every heading, paragraph, button, and form field on the site. The pixel-LCD font never appears in a sentence — only as numerals (clock) or a proper name (the bot's identity in the chat header).

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest everywhere. A shadow may appear only as a hover/focus response (service cards); it never describes a resting state, and no drop shadows, glassmorphism, or gradient-as-depth are used elsewhere (the header's backdrop-blur is translucency, not elevation).

dos: Do keep Signal Lime (#B8FF5B) to one resting-state element per screen; use hover/active/selected states to let it appear more than once, never two simultaneous primary CTAs.
Do build every new panel from the three-tone stack (Paper #F9F9F9 / Console #171717 / Void #000000) rather than introducing a fourth background tone.
Do default every new surface to flat; only add a shadow as a hover or focus response, and only on card-like elements that already lift (-translate-y-1 pattern).
Do use pill shape (rounded-full) for every button and chip; reserve 16–20px radii for cards, panels, and images.
Do keep the pixel-LCD font confined to numerals or the bot's proper name; every sentence of real content stays in Space Grotesk.
donts: Don't introduce a second or third accent hue — the palette is one signal color plus neutrals, by design.
Don't add drop shadows, glassmorphism, or gradients as a resting-state depth cue anywhere in the system.
Don't set the pixel-LCD font as body or heading text; it reads as a display glitch outside the clock/bot-name context it was chosen for.
Don't sharpen corners on buttons or cards to less than the established radii — sharp corners break the soft-geometry-on-technical-base read that holds the system together.
